title: The Machine Heard Two Rooms Away
transcript:
Employees at a small design studio had complained for months about a low humming noise. The sound was strongest in a meeting room, yet the machine suspected of causing it stood two rooms away. Closing the intervening doors made little difference, and adding soft wall panels reduced echoes without removing the hum.

An acoustic engineer visiting the studio explained that noise can travel through a building in more than one way. Some sound moves through the air, while vibration can pass through floors, walls and supporting structures. Treating a room as if every unwanted sound arrived through the air may therefore leave the main route untouched.

The engineer measured vibration at several points while the machine was switched on and off. The pattern was strongest along a continuous section of floor connecting the equipment area with the meeting room. A metal support attached to the machine was transferring vibration directly into that surface. The walls between the rooms were not the principal problem.

The studio tested a revised mounting arrangement designed to reduce this transfer. The improvement was noticeable during ordinary operation, but the engineer also checked the machine at its highest working speed. A support that performs well under one condition may behave differently under another. After a small adjustment, the arrangement reduced the disturbance across the range of speeds normally used.

The manager says the investigation prevented further spending on decorative acoustic products that would not have addressed the cause. The wall panels remain useful for conversation inside the meeting room, but they serve a different purpose. The case is a reminder that an uncomfortable sound must first be traced to its path through the building before an effective treatment can be chosen.

questions.prompt: What had the soft wall panels achieved before the engineer’s visit?
options: They stopped the machine from operating.
They removed the low hum completely.
They blocked vibration through the floor.
They reduced echoes but did not remove the hum.
questions.answer: They reduced echoes but did not remove the hum.
questions.explanation: 软墙板减轻了室内回声，却没有消除主要低频嗡声。

questions.prompt: How was the disturbance mainly reaching the meeting room?
options: Through an open window facing the street.
Through vibration transferred into a continuous floor section.
Through conversations in the intervening rooms.
questions.answer: Through vibration transferred into a continuous floor section.
questions.explanation: 机器金属支撑把振动直接传给连通会议室的地板结构。

questions.prompt: Why did the engineer test the revised mounting at the highest working speed?
options: Its performance could differ under different operating conditions.
The staff used that speed only when visitors arrived.
The machine could not be switched off at a lower speed.
The wall panels needed to be removed during the test.
questions.answer: Its performance could differ under different operating conditions.
questions.explanation: 固定装置在不同工况下表现可能不同，不能只验证普通速度。

questions.prompt: What practical lesson did the studio learn?
options: Any sound problem can be solved by closing doors.
Decorative panels should never be used in meeting rooms.
The transmission route should be identified before choosing a treatment.
Machines must always be placed outdoors.
questions.answer: The transmission route should be identified before choosing a treatment.
questions.explanation: 先找出声音传播路径，才能选择针对原因的处理方式。
